entities.summary: James Barron was an officer in the United States Navy. He served in the Quasi-War and the Barbary Wars, during which he commanded a number of famous ships, including USS Essex and USS President. As commander of the frigate USS Chesapeake, in 1807 he was involved in the Chesapeake–Leopard affair, which led to the surrender of his ship to the British and resulted in his court-martial for his actions during the incident. After criticism from some fellow officers, the resulting controversy led Barron to a pistol duel with one of the officers who had presided over his court-martial, Stephen Decatur, resulting in Decatur's death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: James Barron's involvement in the Chesapeake-Leopard affair led to a significant escalation of tensions between the United States and Great Britain, ultimately contributing to the War of 1812. The controversy surrounding his actions also had a lasting impact on naval protocol and officer conduct.
